transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 min
Attendees: Evan Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (DataHarbor CTO), Mark Reynolds (Platform Eng), Alex Wu (SRE)

Auto-summary: align on benchmark harness integration, define success criteria (latency p95 < 250ms for streaming, < 150ms non-streaming, cost per 1M tokens target), collect customer scripts and schedule canary run.

[00:00] Evan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm Evan from Redwood, this is Sofia, our systems eng. how are you all?
[00:10] Priya (CTO): hi all, priya here. excited to dig in, we've got Mark and Alex with me for infra details.
[00:18] Mark (Platform Eng): hey, thanks. our main goal is to validate performance for our user-facing summarization pipeline and chat support flow.
[00:26] Sofia (SE): great. so today's agenda is bench scoping: success critera, workload sizing, harness integration, and timing. also the streaming vs non-streaming thing keeps coming up so we'll cover that.
[00:34] Alex (SRE): quick note - security and VPC constraints are must-haves for us, and we need KMS integration for any private deploys.
[00:41] Evan (AE): noted. ok first — success criteria. what does a pass look like for DataHarbor?
[00:49] Priya (CTO): for the summarization, we need p95 latency under 250ms for streaming response mode, and for batch non-streaming inference under 150ms; quality must match our current baseline (rouge/bleu-ish metrics) within a small delta. cost target is important too — ideally less than 60% of our current per-token cost.
[01:12] Sofia (SE): when you say streaming p95 < 250ms, are you measuring to first token or to final token?
[01:18] Priya (CTO): to first meaningful token, because UX requires fast start.
[01:24] Mark (Platform Eng): also concurrency - our peak concurrent sessions is around 1,200 active users for web, moving to 3k during big events. so harness needs to model that.
[01:36] Evan (AE): good. workload sizing — average session length, tokens per session?
[01:40] Alex (SRE): avg session 320 tokens total, but distribution is heavy tail — 80% under 400, 10% over 1k. we will provide histograms.
[01:52] Sofia (SE): perfect, that helps sizing. for throughput tests we usually run RPS profiles + arrival distributions, and include warm/cold KV-cache scenarios.
[02:02] Priya (CTO): what's your KV-cache behavior? we use a prefix cache to accelerate repeated contexts.
[02:08] Sofia (SE): Redwood does prefix/KV cache; in Dedicated we can pin cache warmers to keep hot keys in memory; for hosted we have eviction depending on workload. note: transcription sometimes says 'K-V cache' or 'K-V cash' in our reports.
[02:22] Mark (Platform Eng): another constraint — our data residency requirements mean any private deploy needs to be in our EU region and must be behind our V-P-C.
[02:30] Evan (AE): yep ok. security checkboxes (SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS) — we'll attach our security pack.
[02:36] Priya (CTO): please include audit log retention details.
[02:40] Evan (AE): will do.
[02:43] Sofia (SE): on harness integration: we have a reference benchmark harness (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness) that supports streaming and non-streaming modes. we can run the customer-provided traffic scripts against hosted or dedicated endpoints.
[02:58] Mark (Platform Eng): what's the preferred method to run these from our side? we run everything in k8s and prefer a simple helm chart or docker-compose.
[03:06] Sofia (SE): the harness provides a docker image and a k8s job manifest. we can also give a minimal helm chart. for on-prem we accept an SSH runner approach too.
[03:16] Alex (SRE): do you support websocket streaming and SSE? our client uses websockets for real-time responses.
[03:22] Sofia (SE): yes, streaming is supported via websockets and SSE both. just note behavior differences: websocket keeps a persistent conn, so load shaping is different vs HTTP chunked responses. we'll include churn tests.
[03:36] Priya (CTO): we want to compare streaming vs non-streaming because our UX might benefit from lower time-to-first-token even if cost increases. can you measure both first-token latency and completion latency?
[03:48] Sofia (SE): absolutely. harness will capture time-to-first-token, token-throughput, and end-to-end completion. we'll also measure CPU/GPU utilization, VRAM pressure, and per-token latency distribution.
[03:59] Evan (AE): on quality, we'll need you to provide evaluation prompts and reference outputs. do you have a labeled eval set?
[04:06] Priya (CTO): yes, we'll share a 500-example eval set with expected outputs and accept small variance. scoring is approximate.
[04:13] Mark (Platform Eng): can the harness replay sessions with timing fidelity? we need to model think time.
[04:18] Sofia (SE): yes, the runner supports inter-arrival times and variable think time distributions. we'll want your session traces.
[04:26] Alex (SRE): what about model variants and quantization? we plan to test a few options — float32 baseline and int8 quantized variants.
[04:34] Sofia (SE): the harness supports model variant switching; we'll note that quantized models may affect latency and quality. we'll produce a report that includes quality regression alerts.
[04:45] Priya (CTO): do you do auto-batching? our workload has lots of short requests and batching can help cost but might harm latency.
[04:53] Sofia (SE): Redwood's runtime uses dynamic batching with latency SLO knobs; harness can toggle batch sizes and measure impact. we can run experiments: 1) aggressive batching for cost, 2) conservative for latency, 3) hybrid with latency SLO enforcement.
[05:10] Evan (AE): let's talk timelines. recommended flow: 1) exchange scripts and runbook this week, 2) Redwood prepares a canary run on a small dedicated instance w/ your eval set, 3) full-scale run week of 2026-04-13. sound realistic?
[05:27] Priya (CTO): yes, we can get scripts by 2026-04-02; do you have any constraints on data sanitization?
[05:33] Evan (AE): we'll accept sanitized traces; if anything sensitive we'll run in your VPC/dedicated environment.
[05:38] Mark (Platform Eng): cost reporting — we need token-level breakdowns and GPU utilization timeline.
[05:44] Sofia (SE): harness will emit per-request metrics, and Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns. we'll attach sample dashboards.
[05:53] Alex (SRE): what about failure modes — do you simulate OOMs, slow nodes?
[05:58] Sofia (SE): yes we include churn/failure injection tests; also fallback policies for model variants if capacity constrained.
[06:06] Priya (CTO): one more — do you support HSM-backed KMS for key management?
[06:11] Evan (AE): yes, enterprise private supports HSM/KMS integration; we'll include security docs.
[06:16] Mark (Platform Eng): can you run the harness from our k8s cluster while calling Redwood Hosted endpoints? we'd like the load origin to be within our VPC to mimic egress restrictions.
[06:27] Sofia (SE): yes, that's supported — runner can live in your cluster, and we can provide endpoint credentials and firewall guidance. note that if you require private connectivity for hosted we'd need to review networking options.
[06:39] Priya (CTO): ok great. on success criteria recap: p95 streaming to first-token < 250ms, non-streaming p95 < 150ms, quality within delta, cost target < 60% of current.
[06:52] Evan (AE): perfect — i'll capture that in the runbook.
[06:56] Sofia (SE): any blockers we should know about?
[07:00] Priya (CTO): only that our legal team requires a short security questionnaire answered before we run hosted tests.
[07:07] Evan (AE): we'll send that with the security pack.
[07:11] Mark (Platform Eng): for the harness — we'll provide a representative 3 scripts: 1) summarization (avg 320 tokens), 2) chat session (avg 150 tokens), 3) long-form doc condense (avg 750 tokens).
[07:23] Alex (SRE): also include sample concurrency traces.
[07:26] Evan (AE): noted. i'll email the repo and the runbook by monday 2026-03-29.
[07:33] Priya (CTO): we'll aim to upload scripts by 2026-04-02.
[07:37] Sofia (SE): i'll schedule a 30-minute canary run coordination call for 2026-04-09 or 04-10 to align infra.
[07:45] Evan (AE): ok recap of next steps: share harness + runbook; customer provides scripts; schedule canary; run full-scale week of 2026-04-13. any other items?
[07:55] Priya (CTO): no, that's it. thanks everyone.
[08:00] Evan (AE): thanks, we'll follow up in email with links — benchmark harness repo, runbook, security pack, and a sample dashboard.

Notes on transcript quality: minor transcription errors (Redwood Dedicatedy, K-V cache, V-P-C) and occasional speaker mislabels. Links referenced: harness repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness), security pack (https://redwood.ai/security-pack), sample dashboard (https://redwood.ai/dashboards/sample).

End of transcript.
